meta.disclaimer: Factual planning awareness — not a substitute for official advisories or common-sense precautions. Conditions vary by city, route, and season.

intro: Most independent travellers visit Southern Africa without incident. These are the practical pitfalls self-drivers and first-time safari visitors ask about most — so you can plan around them.

topics.title: USD note condition
topics.body: Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe, and many borders reject torn, marked, or pre-2006 USD notes. Carry crisp bills from a bank or forex bureau — not change from a previous border.

topics.title: ATM & card skimming
topics.body: Use ATMs inside banks or malls in cities. Avoid isolated machines at night. Notify your bank of travel dates. Have a backup card — Mastercard more widely accepted than Amex in the region.

topics.title: Unofficial border 'helpers'
topics.body: Touts offer to speed paperwork for a fee. Use official counters only. Never hand passports to anyone except uniformed immigration officers. Know your visa category before the window.

topics.title: Night driving
topics.body: Wildlife, livestock, pedestrians, and unlit trucks make night driving the highest-risk activity for self-drivers. Plan to reach camp by sunset — especially Namibia, Botswana, and Zambia.

topics.title: Fuel & cash planning
topics.body: Remote routes run out of fuel and card terminals fail. Namibia north of Etosha, Mozambican EN1 stretches, and Malawian lakeshore roads need full tanks and reserve jerry cans where legal.

topics.title: Over-trusting lodge Wi‑Fi
topics.body: Do not rely on camp Wi‑Fi for banking or urgent bookings. Load offline maps, boarding passes, and PDF confirmations before leaving town.

topics.title: Malaria assumption errors
topics.body: Travellers skip prophylaxis for Cape Town then fly to Luangwa the same trip. Check every destination and season — malaria zones do not follow country borders.

topics.title: Lake & river hazards
topics.body: Bilharzia in Lake Malawi shallow bays; crocodiles and hippos at shorelines at dusk. Ask locals before swimming — 'clear' water is not always safe.

topics.title: Vehicle break-ins
topics.body: Do not leave bags visible in rental cars in cities and at viewpoints. Trunk packing before reaching trailheads. Victoria Falls and Cape Town car parks — take valuables.

topics.title: Rental cross-border paperwork
topics.body: Assuming a South African rental includes Zimbabwe or Botswana without a letter is the most expensive border mistake. Get written permission and COMESA cover before departure.
